**Eicher Motors (Royal Enfield)**
- Siddhartha Lal joined and became Royal Enfield CEO around 2000. The brand was "barely trudging along" with stagnant sales before the product reboot (repositioned controls, more powerful models) — [Business Standard](https://business-standard.com/amp/article/companies/ceo-of-the-year-racing-ahead-117031700863_1.html); [Medium/Finception](https://medium.com/finception/eicher-motors-from-good-to-great-69bab6ca47a2)
- Eicher was the Fastest Wealth Creator in Motilal Oswal's 19th study (2009–14). Eicher, Supreme Industries and Page Industries were in the top 10 fastest — [MOSL WC study 2009-14](https://www.motilaloswal.com/content/dam/mofsl-website-adobe/investor-relations/wealth-creation/wc19.pdf)
- From April 2005 at about ₹32 adjusted to about ₹2,754, an 86x gain, by the time of PrimeInvestor's article — [PrimeInvestor, "A multi-bagger that no one foresaw"](https://primeinvestor.in/?p=56537). Recent price about ₹7,630 (7 Sep 2026; 52-week range ₹6,411–8,230) — [Kotak Neo](https://www.kotakneo.com/stocks/eicher-motors-ltd/). Note: the pre-2020 price (around ₹27,000–30,000) was before the 2020 10:1 split, so "₹30,000" is the unadjusted peak-era price.

**Defence PSUs (HAL, BEL, Mazagon Dock, Cochin Shipyard)**
- July 2023: the rally in defence stocks was "largely driven by valuation rerating rather than faster growth in revenue and profit" — [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/rally-in-listed-defence-stocks-yet-to-be-backed-by-earnings-growth-123071300913_1.html)
- Elara linked the rerating to the rising share of indigenisation and to export opportunities — [Business Standard May 2024](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/defense-stocks-on-roll-bdl-bel-hal-cochin-shipyard-rally-5-124051800383_1.html)
- April 2025 multiples versus history: HAL 28.4x one-year-forward P/E against a 5-year average of 14x. BEL 40.8x against 20.7x. Mazagon Dock 29.7x against a 3-year average of 16.6x — [Business Today/Nirmal Bang](https://businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/mazagon-dock-hal-bdl-bel-share-price-targets-for-9-defence-stocks-ahead-of-q4-results-471974-2025-04-15). Multiples roughly doubled against history.

body: The core ingredients (cross-sectional momentum, time-series momentum/trend following, the 52-week-high effect, and post-earnings-announcement drift) are among the most robust anomalies in finance, including in India. Chart patterns and indicator rules have much weaker, era- and data-snooping-sensitive evidence. Meanwhile, base rates for active retail traders are grim: ~88-93% of Indian F&O traders lose money each year, 97% of persistent Brazilian day traders lost money, and <1% of Taiwanese day traders are predictably profitable.

body:
1. FY23 CFO/PAT = 115/23 = **5.0**, and FCF/PAT = −324/23 = **−14.1**. CFO looked strong because of the working-capital release that year: working-capital days went from 132 to −9, consistent with customer advances or payables. Capex of ₹439 cr was being bought with debt.
2. Under Ind AS 116, aircraft lease repayments (principal and interest) sit in CFF, not CFO, so CFO overstates the cash the operations generate. CFF of −21,276 is mostly lease and debt servicing, which is an unavoidable operating cost for an airline. Lease-adjusted FCF is roughly 23,470 − 1,703 − ~20,000 ≈ **near zero**. (Approximate; take the lease-payment line from the annual report's cash-flow note.)
3. $2.5 bn. That is about **54x** FY25 CFO of −$46 m in absolute size, and roughly 29% of FY25 revenue. The programme is existential-scale.
4. 500 − 180 − 120 = **₹200 cr**. The headline CFO was 2.5x the comparable figure.

body:
- A principal books the gross sale price. An agent books only the commission.
- The test is whether the company **controls** the good before transfer: inventory risk, pricing discretion and primary responsibility.
- Gross-up does not change profit, but it inflates revenue, distorts margins, turnover and P/S, and it is a favourite way to "grow" ahead of an IPO.

**Worked example H: Eternal (ETERNAL), FY25 to FY26.**
- Consolidated revenue went from 20,243 to 54,364 (+169%). TTM revenue is 77,956.
- Blinkit moved to an owned-inventory model, so it now books the full value of goods instead of a marketplace commission.
- Like-for-like, management reported Q3 FY26 group growth of about 64–66% YoY against about 173% reported.
- OPM fell from 3.1% to 2.2% mechanically.
- **Lesson:** on any business-model change, value the company on gross order value, net revenue or contribution, not on reported revenue. Never compare P/S across the change.
- Classic US agent-vs-principal disputes: Groupon (2011 S-1 restated to net revenue after SEC comments) and travel OTAs.

body:
- Under Ind AS 38 / IAS 38, development cost **must** be capitalised once technical feasibility, intent, ability, future benefit and measurability are shown. US GAAP ASC 730 **expenses** R&D, with narrow software exceptions (ASC 350-40, 985-20).
- An Indian auto or pharma company can therefore report higher EBITDA and EPS than a US peer with the same R&D cash.
- **Tests:**
  - capitalised development / total R&D spend over time
  - amortisation period against product life
  - "intangible assets under development" ageing (also a Schedule III requirement)
- Goodwill is not amortised under either system (impairment test only). Watch for impairment tests with high terminal growth or low discount rates, which the auditor's CAM or Key Audit Matter will name.
- **Rule:** if goodwill plus intangibles exceed equity, compute tangible book value and ROCE on tangible capital as well.

| REI Agro (liquidation 2017) | REIAGROLTD | yes | 2006–2016 | yes | no |
| Innoventive Industries (first IBC case, 2017) | 533402 (404) → INNOIND | yes | to 2016 | yes | no |
| Tecpro Systems (NSE compulsory delisting 2018) | TECPRO | yes | to 2014 | no (stopped filing) | no |
| Deccan Chronicle (NSE compulsory delisting 2017) | DCHL | yes | to 2014 | no | no |
| GEI Industrial Systems (compulsory delisting 2018) | GEINDSYS | yes | old | no | no |
| Indus Fila (compulsory delisting 2019) | INDUSFILA | yes | to 2016 | yes | no |
| Bhushan Steel (IBC-resolved, then merged) | BHUSANSTL | **404** | – | – | – |
| Monnet Ispat (IBC-resolved, renamed) | MONNETISPA | **404** | – | – | – |

**13 of 15 dead firms have a screener page (87%)** → above the 50% stop line; the test proceeds. The two misses are
IBC-resolved companies that were later renamed or merged (their page now lives under the new name or is gone). Every
page also serves a weekly, split- and bonus-adjusted price series (checked on Infosys around its Sep-2018 1:1 bonus:
continuous at ~₹700) and screener's market-cap-to-sales series, through `/api/company/<id>/chart/`, even after the
stock stopped trading (Era Infra's series ends 12-Sep-2016). Schedules (`/api/company/<id>/schedules/`) also work for
dead firms (Murli Industries' borrowings to Mar-2016). Some dead firms simply stopped filing *before* the snapshot
(Tecpro, Deccan Chronicle): they are correctly not in the universe at T (not live filers).
